steps.text: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat. Stir in garlic and flour; cook and stir until garlic is fragrant but not brown, about 1 minute.
Whisk in heavy cream and milk until mixture is hot and slightly thickened, about 10 minutes. Gradually stir in Parmesan cheese and fontina cheese. Season with salt and pepper.
Continue to simmer until cheese melts and sauce thickens, stirring often, 20 to 30 more minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Buttery Alfredo Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This buttery Alfredo sauce recipe makes a rich, creamy, Italian-style sauce that’s rich with Parmesan and fontina cheeses. Serve with chicken or pasta.

video.description: This is a rich, creamy, Italian-style Alfredo sauce perfect for chicken and seafood pastas! It has a wonderful blend of fontina and Parmesan cheeses that give this traditional flavor. The secret to this alfredo sauce is that it doesn’t have cream cheese!

review.reviewBody:
This is by far better than other alfredo sauces I have tried - those end up being greasy or the butter and cream separating. I used real parmagiano-reggiano and asiago instead of fontina. 

I served this with farfalle pasta, grilled chicken breasts that were thinly sliced, 6 slices of julienned bacon that I rendered until crisp, I sauteed chopped onion and the minced garlic in the bacon drippings -- drained all of those and set it aside. I also diced 3 roma tomatoes and wahed 3 cups of fresh baby spinach. 

I made the alfredo sauce in a large, deep skillet and when it was done I added the al dente pasta. Then I added the sliced chicken breast, bacon, onions, garlic, tomatoes and spinach. I stirred the ingredients until combined, covered the skillet and brought it up to temperature on low heat, stirring occasionally until the spinach was wilted. 

Delicious doesn't even come close to describing the meal - much better than I've eaten at any chain Italian restaurant... and the sauce was the star!!

OMG! I knew this was greatness after my first taste. I omitted the fontina cheese and used a Parmesan, Romano, asiago blend instead and salted butter. Otherwise I followed the recipe exactly; cutting everything in half to make a smaller portion. I felt like a rock star when I was done, and I was stuffed when my bowl was empty. I put the sauce on farfalle pasta with grilled chicken, spinach and mushrooms. This was better than what I would have gotten in a restaurant. Now when I have a craving for some pasta Alfredo, I can just make it at home. I can't wait to try it with some shrimp and fettuccine. This really is a fabulous recipe.

I am an alfredo sauce junkie and I absolutely LOVED this recipe! This is by far the best alfredo sauce I've had (including fancy Italian places). Definitely very rich (ok, fattening!)and should be reserved for special occasions, but SO worth it! I made crab alfredo using this sauce for my new husband on Valentines's Day and it was perfect! Nothing says "I love you" like crab alfredo! Thanks for the recipe!

This was very good. I did 1/4 of the recipe since I only needed a small amount. Added several good twists of freshly ground sea salt and black pepper and several dashes of dried basil; left out the fontina and used a little water instead of the whole milk. Also used 1 clove garlic, finely chopped, instead of minced garlic. Delicious!! :)

I have been looking for a recipe like this for decades! I have been trying to emulate the alfredo sauce from my favorite Italian restsurant, but could never get it quite right.....until I found this recipe. You need look no further if you want out-of-this-world alfredo sauce! This sauce is the real deal. If you are going to have "heart attack on a plate," you may as well spoil yourself and go with the best. I stirred a bag of fresh spinach into the sauce and served it over fettuccine noodles. So rich and so filling. Thank you for submitting this recipe.
THIS IS GREAT! I just added 3 tablespoon of fresh pesto and a 1/2 teaspoon of nutmeg

Amazing! Since I was only making it for two, I made 1/4 of the recipe and I still have leftovers. This is the best Alfredo I've ever tasted. Also, I did not find it necessary to simmer it an extra 20-30 min. I took it off the heat, then added the cheese and all the cheese melted just fine. Oh, I used asiago cheese in place of both cheeses so maybe that made a difference.

My goodness, this is delicious! I’m glad I chose this recipe to try! There were only a couple things I had to change. I cut the recipe in half (because it’s just me eating it) and used salted butter. I also used corn starch instead of flour, because I have celiacs and can’t have gluten. For this, I did 1 TBLS of corn starch mixed with a little bit of water, and poured the mixture in with the cream. For the cheese, I did a Parmesan/ Romano cheese mix (it was on sale), along with the fontina. This is restaurant grade sauce! For the complete meal, I mixed mushrooms and spinach into the sauce, and had it with sautéed shrimp and chicken over some gluten free rotini. I stuffed myself, it was so good!

The base recipe itself tastes AMAZING! I did tweak it just a tad by adding fresh mushrooms, though. I would make one minor adjustment to the overall recipe, whether you add mushrooms or not.....add just a little more flour, as the consistency was a bit thin.

I made this for my husbands birthday dinner, and instead of traditional fettuccine pasta, I made it with three cheese tortellini, served with grilled chicken breast. I think I could have ate the sauce alone, though, because it was so delicious!


*Edit: I've noticed in a few reviews where people complain that the parm doesn't melt and/or leaves a gritty texture; make sure you use FRESH parmesan and shred it yourself....not the stuff in a jar.

I made this for the first time last night and it was great!! Added a few things... When I added the garlic, I also added onions. I couldn't find fontina cheese so I used muenster cheese. Finally, I had some left over chicken, so I chopped it up and threw that in too. Served it over fettuccine noodles, with one of my green bean recipes as a side dish, and the family just about licked their bowls. I'll have to agree with tami1968, this is a very rich recipe so I'll have to use it on special occasions or find another recipe not so high in fat.

Because of the reviews, I only used 1/2cup of butter (1stick). I used an 8oz wedge of parm and a 5oz wedge of fontina. I shredded them finely. I ended up adding and additional tablespoon of flour. The sauce did not separate. I refrigerated the leftover sauce, it basically became solid. Reheated on the stove on low, it reheated beautifully. The best Alfredo sauce I’ve ever had! Oh, I served it over angel hair pasta with fried eggplant and pan grilled thin chicken breast, delish!

I can't for the life of me figure out why all the Alfredo sauce recipes call for so much butter. I made this one with only 25 % of the butter it calls for and it was the best recipe yet.i like butter but not an overwhelming amount . I'm sure there is a reason I can't figure what it is .
Sooo good! I add chicken, shrimp and cajun sausage in mine. Delicious 😋
This alfredo sauce was amazing. The recipe was super easy to follow. I will definitely make it again.

4.5 stars for a classic, Alfredo sauce (but I am rounding up). This makes A LOT! I should have known better and halved it but figured - why not? Oh my! I have enough Alfredo sauce for 2, if not 3 meals for four people. This would be great if you plan on having a small party with a pasta bar! I followed exactly and served over cheese ravioli. I plan to make again for an Alfredo lasagna again sometime this week. This is rich yet not overwhelming. Would recommend and will make again. Thanks Crystal R Ward!
Excellent recipe, simple and clear instructions, I love the result. Sometimes I dice a chicken breast or two and add to the sauce, but it works just as well without.
Absolutely great
This was absolutely AMAZING!
Been told several times it was the best alfredo my guests have ever had
Favorite Alfredo sauce! Family loves this recipe. I have to double the the recipe because they live to dip their bread sticks in it.
